//: Texture budgets per surface. TWO ceilings, because they fail differently.
//transfer: Bytes on the wire. Binds on school wifi. What a file size tells you.
//vram: Bytes resident once decoded. Binds on a school Chromebook, and is the one that actually breaks things: an upload is RGBA8 whatever the file said, so a 4 MB compressed asset can be 64 MB resident. A budget stated only in transfer bytes cannot see that.
//maxDimension: Hard ceiling on any single texture edge. Above a device's MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE a texture does not degrade, it fails to bind — a black sky, not a softer one. Commonly 4096 on low-end Chromebooks, so 8192 is already optimistic and needs the runtime check plus a real fallback tier.

timemap.description: A teacher's research tool. The fleet's primary and only default surface.
timemap.//cloud-patches: The cloud deck's detail source: six MODIS patches at 611 m per texel, tiled stochastically. Each is a 4x4 block of z8 tiles covering the same 626 km of sky one z6 tile did, so 3072x2048 is sixteen times the texels over identical ground — 32 MiB resident with mipmaps, against 2 MiB at z6. That is the single largest texture on this surface and it is bought deliberately: Bart's verdict on the coarse version was 'this is not HQ clouds', and at 2446 m per texel the deck was four times coarser than the ground beneath it.
timemap.//cloud-patches-ceiling: z8 is the LAST step a single baked atlas can take. z9 would be 306 m per texel, 2048 per patch, a 6144x4096 atlas at 128 MiB resident — over this surface's entire 96 MiB ceiling on its own, before the field, the wind, the Milky Way or the moon. Past z8 the answer is not a bigger bake, it is streaming only the sky being looked at.
timemap.//cloud-field: clouds-field.webp stays alongside it and is NOT redundant. It is the real global DISTRIBUTION of cloud at 19.5 km per texel; the atlas is placeless detail. The deck needs both — the atlas alone puts cloud on 74% of the disc against a true 26%.

lesson-map.description: The lesson map has one ground and it is the Earth, so the globe is no longer opt-in per lesson — but what it may spend still is. resolveQuality('lessonMap') decides at runtime and addGlobeLayers never creates a layer the plan refused, so the asset is not fetched rather than fetched and hidden. This surface had ~1 MB of glyph chunks and three tilesets removed for cold-load time; the ceilings below are unchanged from when it was opt-in and do not get raised to fit new work.
lesson-map.//declared: What a CAPABLE device actually loads here, which is what this list has to state or the check is a false green. SURFACES.lessonMap asks for sky, relief and ocean only: the sun disc, the cloud deck and the orbits are dropped as out of scope on every machine, so they are not this surface's cost and are not listed. The sky texture is halved to 4096 against the 1 MB single-asset ceiling before it is allowed in. A weaker device or a metered connection gets less again, and the Globe layers panel greys what it cannot have.
lesson-map.//not-listed: cloud-patches.webp is the reason this note exists. At 1.8 MB it is over the single-asset ceiling on its own and the surface never asks for it, so it must never appear here — if a future change puts clouds on the lesson map, this budget is what should stop it, and adding the file to this list to make the check pass would be defeating the instrument rather than reading it.

landing-hero.description: First paint. Loaded after paint, never blocking.

optional.//: Reachable but not loaded by default, so outside the surface totals. Listed so the dimension rule still applies and so nothing is silently untracked.
optional.//relief: earth-normal-8192.webp arrived with `realistic-earth` and is OPTIONAL for a measured reason, not because nobody got round to declaring it. At 8192x4096 it is 128 MiB resident before mipmaps and 171 MiB with them, against a 96 MiB surface ceiling — so it cannot be a default-on layer at this size, whatever the 3.6 MiB file size suggests. It is exactly the case the vram ceiling above exists to catch. Today only the measurement harness loads it (`daylight.js` defaults reliefUrl to null and nothing in the app sets it), and the layers panel ships its relief toggle OFF for the same reason. Moving it into `timemap` needs a smaller bake or a quality tier that picks one, not an edit to this list.

scan.//: A budget only sees what it is told about. Without this, a texture nobody declares passes silently — the same shape as every other bug this programme has produced: correct for the reader who added it, invisible to everyone downstream. So the directories are scanned and anything undeclared FAILS. Declaring an asset is then a deliberate act with a surface attached, rather than the default being untracked.
scan.//later: The honest version derives the asset list from the code that loads it. That waits until the tile pyramid stops the asset set moving; this is the cheap 80% that needs only a directory listing.
